landing.metaTitle: Root house — Create the living story of your family
landing.metaDescription: A private family archive: your tree, photos, stories and relatives' voices in one place. Gather your family's story together — start for free.
landing.brandStatement: Create the living story of your family.
landing.demoNote: The Hartleys are fictional. Photos are archival and in the public domain.

hero.lead: From your earliest known ancestor to your children — on one line, with photos, places and stories.

how.title: Three steps, and your family has its archive.

people.title: Add yourself and your relatives
people.body: Start with yourself, then parents and grandparents. The tree arranges itself.

memories.title: Fill it with memories
memories.body: Photos, stories, dates, places and voice recordings — everyone gets their own page.

family.title: Invite the people who remember
family.body: Relatives add what you don't know. Everyone sees the same story.

landing.showcaseTitle: A person is more than a name and two dates.

tree.title: A family tree that grows with you
tree.body: Add people one by one and the tree arranges itself: partners side by side, children under their parents, every branch where you'd expect it.

profile.title: A page for every person
profile.body: Where they were born and lived, what they did, the photos they're in and the stories about them — all on one page.

photos.title: Photos that know who's in them
photos.body: Tag people in an old photo and it shows up on each of their pages. Hover over a face to see who it is.

stories.title: Stories to read and to listen to
stories.body: Write down a family story and link it to everyone who was there. Listen to it in a relative's recorded voice or your device's voice.

lifeline.title: Lifeline
lifeline.body: Births, moves, weddings and everything in between — on one line from the first year to the last.

kinship.title: How are we related?
kinship.body: Pick any two people and see the path between them — and what to call each other.

panel.moveStory: Ivan found work at the port; Vera followed with the children's things in two suitcases.

together.title: A family's story shouldn't rest on one person's memory.
together.lead: Invite your relatives — each adds what they remember. And you decide who sees and can change what.

private.title: Private by default
private.body: Every family archive is its own closed space. Nothing becomes public unless you choose it.

roles.title: Clear roles
roles.body: Owner, editor, contributor, viewer — everyone gets exactly the access they need.

invite.title: Invitation only
invite.body: Relatives join by personal invitation. There's no open sign-up into an archive.

share.title: Share on your terms
share.body: Keep a person, photo or story to yourself, or show it through a separate link — with a password if you like.

pricing.title: A plan for every family
pricing.lead: Start for free and switch plans when you need more space or more members.

who.a: Only the people you invite into your family archive. Everything is private by default; you can show a single person, photo or story through a link — with a password if you like.

export.q: Can I take my photos with me?
export.a: Yes — you can download the original of any photo in full quality. Exporting the whole archive as one file is in the works.

elders.q: What if my relatives aren't good with technology?
elders.a: The link in the invitation is all they need. The Viewer role can only look around, and any story can simply be listened to.

problem.title: Everyone holds a piece of the story.
problem.body: Photos live on phones. Stories live in relatives' memories. Names hide in old documents. And the important details often survive only in conversation.

storyPage.lead: In the spring of '52 Grandpa worked at the Riga port, and on Saturdays he went dancing by the Daugava. That's where he first saw Grandma.

privacyPolicy.metaDescription: What data Root house collects, why, who can see it and how to delete it.
privacyPolicy.title: Privacy policy
privacyPolicy.intro: Root house is a private family archive. It holds the most personal things: photographs, memories, details about your relatives. So here it is, short and without fine print: what we collect, why, who sees it and how to delete it.

operator.title: Who is responsible for your data
operator.p1: The Root house service and its team. For any question about your data, write to <email></email> — we reply within 30 days.

data.title: What we collect
data.account: Account: name, email, profile photo (when you sign in with Google), interface language. Your password is stored only as a cryptographic hash — not even we can read it.
data.archive: Archive content: people and family relationships, dates, events, places, stories, photos, audio recordings and documents that you and your relatives add.
data.photos: Information inside photos: the original is stored as uploaded, with whatever the camera recorded (date taken, sometimes location). The smaller copies shown in the archive carry none of it.
data.technical: Technical data: your sign-in session, the family activity log (who added or changed what — visible to family members), and server logs, including IP addresses, to protect against outages and abuse.
data.analytics: Visit statistics: anonymous — which pages are opened, on what devices and from which countries, how fast the site loads. No advertising cookies, no cross-site tracking. The secret parts of invitation and share links are removed in your browser before anything is sent.

purpose.title: Why
purpose.p1: Only to run the service: store and show your archive, let in the people you invited, send invitations, keep accounts safe and learn what to improve. We don't sell data, don't show ads and don't use your photos, stories or details about your relatives to train AI.

access.title: Who sees your archive
access.family: Family members — only the people invited, and only within their role: owner, editor, contributor, viewer. Individual entries can be hidden even from them.
access.links: People with a link — only what you shared through a separate link, and only while it is active. A link can be password-protected.
access.team: The Root house team sees only service information: email, sign-up and last sign-in dates, number of families and entries, storage used. We don't look through archive content, and there is no "sign in as user" feature. Direct database access is used only to fix outages, at your request or when required by law.

processors.title: Service providers
processors.p1: The service runs on infrastructure from companies that process data only on our behalf and never for their own purposes. Their servers may be located outside your country, including in the US and the EU.
processors.vercel: Vercel — hosting, photo and file storage, visit statistics.
processors.google: Google — sign-in with a Google account, if you choose it. We receive only your name, email and profile photo.
processors.resend: Resend — sending invitation emails: the recipient's email and the inviter's name.
processors.maptiler: MapTiler — maps and place search: receives search queries and the map area you are viewing.
processors.voice: Your browser — "Listen" reads a story without a recording in your device's voice. Some browsers use their vendor's cloud voices for this.

cookies.title: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.p1: Only what's necessary: a session cookie to keep you signed in and a cookie for your chosen language. Unsaved story drafts are kept in your browser. No advertising or third-party tracking cookies.

relatives.title: Information about relatives
relatives.p1: Archives often include living people who never signed up themselves. When you add them, make sure they don't mind — especially when it comes to photos, health, faith and other sensitive details. If someone finds themselves in another family's archive and wants their details removed, they can write to us: we'll contact the archive's owner and help.

retention.title: Retention and deletion
retention.p1: Data is kept as long as the account or family archive exists. To delete your account, write to <email></email> from the address it is registered with — we'll delete it within 30 days. Archives where you are the only owner are deleted with your account unless you ask us to hand them over to another member. What you added to other families' archives stays with them. Database backups are overwritten automatically within a few weeks.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.p1: At any time you can find out what data we hold about you, correct it, get a copy (original photos can be downloaded right from the archive), delete it or withdraw your consent — just write to us. If you believe we are violating your rights, you may complain to the data protection authority in your country.

security.title: Security
security.p1: Connections are always encrypted (HTTPS), passwords are stored only as hashes, every archive is isolated from the others, and invitations and share links contain long random keys. No protection is absolute, but if something happens to your data, we will tell you.

age.title: Age
age.p1: The service is intended for people over 16. Children are added to the archive by adult family members.

changes.title: Changes
changes.p1: We'll announce significant changes to this policy in advance, in the service or by email. The date of the current version is at the top of the page.

privacyPolicy.consent: By continuing, you agree to the <link>privacy policy</link>.
